# WebCodecs Capability Evidence — Reported Support Is False

The Awtsmoos is beyond every browser capability flag; Awtsmoos.com records what the codec actually did, not what `isConfigSupported()` promised amid the fog.

## Direct runtime evidence
- H.264 baseline `avc1.42001E`, 640×360, 800 kbps, 12fps, `no-preference + quality`: supported=true, 12 frames queued, 0 encoded outputs, `flush()` timed out after about five seconds.
- H.264 `prefer-software + realtime`: supported=true, 3 frames queued, 0 outputs, `flush()` timed out after about four seconds.
- H.264 `prefer-software + quality`: supported=true, 3 frames queued, 0 outputs, `flush()` timed out after about four seconds.
- H.264 `no-preference + realtime`: supported=true, 3 frames queued, 0 outputs, `flush()` timed out after about four seconds.
- VP8 `prefer-software + realtime`: supported=true, 12 frames queued, 0 outputs, `flush()` timed out after about five seconds.
- VP9 `prefer-software + realtime`: supported=true, 12 frames queued, 0 outputs, `flush()` timed out after about five seconds.
- These failures reproduce on the browser main thread as well as in the Animator worker.
- Therefore the defect is not MediaBunny-specific and not worker-specific. The native Chrome `VideoEncoder` primitive is nonfunctional on this host despite positive capability probes.

## Architectural consequence
`VideoEncoder.isConfigSupported()` cannot be treated as sufficient export capability evidence. Production capability discovery must include a tiny real encode-and-flush smoke probe before selecting WebCodecs. The fallback path must not depend on WebCodecs at all.

## NEXT_ACTION
Implement a canonical browser-frame + soundtrack upload bridge into a bounded local ffmpeg proof/export service. Preserve the existing WebCodecs path for environments where a real encode smoke probe succeeds, but use ffmpeg for this verified host.
